Description: A viral infection affecting the respiratory system, causing body temperature to rise as the immune system fights it off.
Precautions:
Rest and stay hydrated
Isolate from others to avoid spreading
Monitor temperature regularly
Seek care if fever exceeds 103°F (39.4°C) or lasts >3 days
Medications: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever/aches (as directed on label); consult a doctor before antivirals
Workout: Avoid exercise until fever resolves; light stretching only once recovered
Diet: Warm fluids, soups, herbal tea, fruits rich in vitamin C

Description: Inflammation of the airways or throat, often from a viral infection, causing irritation and mucus production.
Precautions:
Cover mouth when coughing
Avoid smoke/dust exposure
Stay hydrated
See a doctor if cough persists >2–3 weeks or brings up blood
Medications: Cough suppressants (dextromethorphan) or expectorants (guaifenesin); throat lozenges
Workout: Avoid strenuous activity; gentle walking if energy allows
Diet: Warm liquids, honey with warm water, avoid cold/fried foods

Description: An allergic reaction to airborne particles (pollen, dust, pet dander) causing inflammation of the nasal passages.
Precautions:
Identify and avoid triggers
Keep windows closed during high pollen days
Use air purifiers
Wash bedding regularly
Medications: Antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine); nasal corticosteroid sprays if recommended by a doctor
Workout: Regular exercise is fine; avoid outdoor workouts on high-pollen days
Diet: Anti-inflammatory foods (ginger, turmeric); avoid known allergens

Description: Inflammation of the stomach lining, often from infection, NSAID overuse, or excess acid, causing pain and discomfort.
Precautions:
Avoid spicy/fatty/acidic foods
Limit alcohol and NSAIDs
Eat smaller, frequent meals
See a doctor if pain is severe or persistent
Medications: Antacids, H2 blockers (famotidine), or proton pump inhibitors (as advised by a doctor)
Workout: Light walking; avoid intense core exercises until resolved
Diet: Bland diet (rice, bananas, toast), avoid caffeine/spicy food

Description: Backflow of stomach acid into the esophagus causing burning chest discomfort. Note: chest pain can also signal heart-related issues, so severe or crushing pain needs emergency evaluation.
Precautions:
Avoid lying down right after eating
Elevate head while sleeping
Avoid trigger foods (spicy, fatty, caffeine)
Seek emergency care for sudden severe chest pain, pressure, or pain radiating to arm/jaw
Medications: Antacids or proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole) as directed
Workout: Avoid heavy lifting or intense exercise right after meals
Diet: Smaller meals, avoid citrus/spicy/fried foods, no late-night eating

Description: Degeneration of joint cartilage, commonly from age or overuse, leading to stiffness and pain in the knee joint.
Precautions:
Avoid high-impact activities
Maintain healthy weight to reduce joint stress
Use knee support if needed
Consult a doctor if swelling or instability occurs
Medications: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) for pain/inflammation, as directed
Workout: Low-impact exercise: swimming, cycling, gentle stretching
Diet: Anti-inflammatory diet (omega-3s, leafy greens); avoid excess sugar/processed food
